messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate detected on canary variant 'gpt-lite-v2-canary' in eu-west-1. 5xx rate spiked to 8% over the last 3m, traffic shifted to fallback variant. Auto-fallback triggered.

mike: oncall here, ack. Paging the team. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-fallback

pagerduty-bot: Paging primary on-call: @mike. Incident severity: P1 (customer-impacting).

mike: quick notes — customers reporting increased latency and incorrect completions. Looks like sticky session fallback is routing a subset to an incompatible variant. @anya can you pull routing logs?

anya: pulling logs now. seeing a pattern: canary instances return 502/503 intermittently, smart-routing detects failures and falls back to 'gpt-stable-v1', but sticky-ttl for the fallback affinity is set to 0 in the policy (BAD). sticky-ttl=0 means sessions remain pinned to fallback variant until eviction.

anya: logs: ```
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] route check canary=gpt-lite-v2-canary -> 502
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] fallback to gpt-stable-v1 (affinity-cookie set, ttl=0)
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] continued requests -> stable (compatibility mismatch for some prompts) -> 422/invalid-output
```

ben: oof. that TTL=0 looks like the cause of persistent misrouting. Was there a config change for rollout policy yesterday?

sara: we shipped a policy tweak in the staged rollout yesterday to try sticky-affinity for latency-sensitive paths. I did set ttl=0 for instant stickiness during the experiment, but forgot to add a fallback eviction window. :grimacing:

mike: okay mitigation plan: 1) pause canary rollout so no new traffic to canary 2) evict existing sticky fallback affinity in eu-west-1 3) route all traffic to stable until we fix TTL and compatibility. Can cloudops run eviction and pause?

cloudops: running eviction now. command I used: ```
redwoodctl routing evict --region eu-west-1 --policy canary-fallback --force
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout state set to PAUSED by @mike (via console).

cloudops: eviction finished. Confirmed ~92% of previously sticky sessions cleared. Starting gradual traffic backfill to stable.

anya: I've pushed a temporary hotfix to the routing agent that enforces min-sticky-ttl=30s for fallbacks. Patch id: patch-2026-03-15-01. Will make permanent change in next deployment.

mike: monitoring metrics now. @julie-cs can you check customer tickets/CS alerts for enterprise impact?

julie-cs: flagged 23 support tickets from EU enterprise customers, mostly degraded outputs and slow timeouts. Marking top 5 for direct outreach.

mike: incident-bot, update status?

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> Mitigated. Current 5xx rate back down to 0.8% in eu-west-1. Error-free rate returning to baseline. Next steps: postmortem scheduled, assign owners.

ben: follow-ups: - revert the experimental ttl=0 in the staging policy - add an automated rollback if fallback-affinity persists >60s - add a smoke test for variant-compatibility before routing fallback traffic

anya: will open the PR for policy defaults and add a unit test for affinity TTL. PR: https://redwood.internal/pulls/6743

sara: I'll own the postmortem and customer comms draft. Starting a doc in #postmortems and pinging legal for any required notices.

mike: handing off to night on-call @sara. If anything regresses, escalate to platform-ops. Thanks all. :thanks:

sara: ack, taking postmortem. Adding timeline and impact numbers.

mike: final numbers for the run: peak affected traffic ~2.3% of total requests for the service during the spike window, 23 enterprise tickets, no SLA breaches recorded (still calculating).

incident-bot: Closing this thread for active mitigation. Please move detailed timelines and logs to the postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-15-canary-fallback-ttl

sara: closing notes: retro actions assigned to @anya (policy defaults), @ben (rollback guard), @sara (customer comms). Will follow up with scheduled postmortem in 48h. :spiral_calendar:
